title: AI Beyond the Business Case II: The Bottleneck Has Moved
author: Richard Claydon
summary: Richard Claydon's second field note on AI and leadership asks what happens after AI raises productivity. Opening with a partner facing five polished documents at 16:20 on a Friday, he argues that AI spreads the ability to produce expert-looking work while judgement stays scarce, so the bottleneck moves to assurance. Polish no longer signals how much scrutiny a draft needs, and research such as a study of junior patent lawyers suggests that visible performance can improve faster than independent judgement. Senior experts become the organisation's assurance layer, and human in the loop oversight only works if the human has expertise, context, authority and time. The cost is displaced leadership attention and a weaker pipeline of future experts. Claydon proposes measuring trusted throughput rather than output volume and protecting the practice and feedback through which judgement develops.
points: AI makes production cheaper and wider, but the capacity to judge whether outputs deserve trust does not expand with it, so the bottleneck shifts to senior assurance.
Fluent, structured AI-assisted drafts hide the signals of uncertainty that reviewers once used to decide how deeply to scrutinise work.
Human oversight is only meaningful when the reviewer has expertise, context, independence, authority and time, otherwise review becomes rapid acceptance.
Senior attention spent verifying output is attention not spent developing others, connecting functions and leading change, so enterprise leadership capacity can fall as expert productivity rises.
Leaders should track trusted throughput and separate what a person can produce with AI from what they can independently judge, protecting supervised practice for juniors.
quotes: AI can increase the number of people capable of producing sophisticated-looking work. It can increase the number of tasks they can complete. It can accelerate the speed at which those outputs arrive.
The capacity required to determine whether those outputs deserve to be acted upon does not automatically expand with them.
An obviously junior draft once advertised how much review it needed. A polished AI-assisted draft may require equally deep scrutiny without announcing that requirement anywhere on the page.
Remove those conditions and the human remains visible while the judgement disappears.

A recent randomised study of patent lawyers found that junior lawyers produced stronger work after several months of AI-assisted drafting. When the AI was removed, their unaided professional judgement showed no average improvement.
The organisation saves time in production and then quietly spends senior attention making the accelerated system trustworthy.
An organisation can improve the answer to the first while gradually weakening its future answer to the second.
Expertise-level productivity can rise while enterprise-level leadership capacity falls.
